note: The families this archive follows, and the two grafts that carry almost all its claimed depth. State is derived, not assigned by hand: a line is DRAWN where this archive publishes a chart of it, DRAWABLE where there are enough people to chart and no chart yet, and a ROUTE where there are too few. Where most of a family's people are recorded without a proved join to anyone else, it is a WEB, because that is what the evidence is.

rows.name: The Hornby descent
rows.what: The family tree runs this line back to a Yorkshire castle and an earldom. Six of the fifteen generations are documented to the day; the rest hang on a single unevidenced link.
rows.gap: A legitimate male descent from the 4th Earl is excluded by the peerage record. 71 people reach this archive only through it.

rows.name: The Keele descent
rows.depth: 27 people, all of them behind one link
rows.what: Followed, looked for in the right registers, and found to be wrong.
rows.gap: Kept on the site because a disproved claim is worth more published than deleted.

close: Remove both grafts and 145 people remain, reaching the middle of the eighteenth century. That is the archive's real floor.
